formula_checks.name: totalShares
formula_checks.why: Adding the shares of every purchase is right. But the formula says a missing share figure counts as zero. A broker-linked purchase that arrives with no quantity then silently drops out, and every figure built on the count (cost per share, market value, gain) is understated with no sign anything is missing. That is 'something missing counted as zero'. The registry tag is fine.
formula_checks.should_be: Total shares = the shares of every purchase added up. When any purchase has no share figure (missing, not a number), there is no total: return nothing and let the screen say a purchase is missing its quantity. A recorded 0 is a real 0 and still adds nothing.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic; the brief's rule that something missing is not counted as zero.

formula_checks.name: contractMultiplier
formula_checks.why: One contract of a US listed equity option is 100 shares unless the contract has been adjusted (after a split or special dividend it can deliver, say, 102 shares). Taking the holding's own stated figure when it is above zero and otherwise 100 for an option and 1 for everything else is right. A zero or negative stated figure is rightly ignored. Low: the registry tag MK-XS-I-055 (the account's wrapper) has nothing to do with this function.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard US equity option contract size (100 shares; adjusted contracts state their own deliverable).

formula_checks.name: costBasis
formula_checks.why: Shares × cost per share, summed, × the contract multiplier is the right total cost (an option premium is quoted per share, so contracts × premium × 100 is what was paid). But the formula is silent on a purchase with no cost per share. Holdings transferred in from another broker often arrive with no basis; adding nothing for that lot makes the total look complete when it is not, and it then feeds avgCost, unrealizedGain and totalROI. The figure that uses it (MK-NW-M-032) says it refuses when no purchase price is recorded, so the function should say so too.
formula_checks.should_be: Cost = Σ (shares × cost per share) × multiplier over every purchase. When any purchase holding shares has no cost per share, return nothing (unknown), not a partial total.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic; refusal rule of MK-NW-M-032 ('No purchase price recorded').

formula_checks.name: avgCost
formula_checks.why: Cost ÷ (shares × multiplier) is the right per-share average, and taking an option's multiplier back out is right (its what_it_is_for says 'divided by the shares held', which is loose for options; the formula is the correct one). But '0 when no shares are held' invents a number: the screen figure MK-NW-M-032 'Price paid (average)' would show $0.00, which reads as 'paid nothing', and its own refusal rule says no number when no purchase price is recorded. It also inherits costBasis's silence on a lot with no cost, which would give an average that is too low.
formula_checks.should_be: Average price paid = cost ÷ (shares held × multiplier), kept unrounded and shown to two decimals. No answer (refuse) when no shares are held or when any lot holding shares has no cost.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0264 / DEC-0310 (full precision, round once); refusal rule of MK-NW-M-032.

formula_checks.name: marketValue
formula_checks.why: Shares × price × multiplier is right when there is a price. '0 when there is no price' is not: a holding with shares and no price is worth something we do not know, not $0. Shown as $0, it drops out of every total and makes the person look poorer; fed into unrealizedGain it would read as a total loss (the next card hides that with its own 0). Elsewhere the app already treats an unpriced holding as unknown: MK-NW-F-127 says a holding that holds something with no price history has a gain that 'cannot be known', and MK-NW-F-128 falls back to the broker's last mark or the value it was built at. This card does neither.
formula_checks.should_be: Market value = shares × price × multiplier when there is a price. With no price: no answer (unknown), so the caller can fall back to the broker's last mark or a hand-built value (MK-NW-F-128) or say the holding is unpriced.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: something missing is not counted as zero; consistency with MK-NW-F-127 / MK-NW-F-128.

formula_checks.name: unrealizedGain
formula_checks.why: Market value − cost is the right since-purchase gain, and it agrees with the 'bought inside the period' branch of MK-NW-F-091 / MK-NW-F-127 (value − cost); those cards' other branches measure a different thing (the gain over a window), so there is no clash there. The fault is '0 when there is no price': the gain of a holding with no price is unknown, and $0 says 'no gain'. It also inherits costBasis's silence on a lot with no cost, which turns that lot's whole value into gain. It also disagrees with capGains (MK-PF-F-006), which skips a lot with no cost: for the same holding the two give different total gains.
formula_checks.should_be: Unrealised gain = market value − cost. No answer when there is no price, or when any lot holding shares has no cost on record.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: missing is not zero; agreement with MK-PF-F-006 totalGain.

formula_checks.name: capGains
formula_checks.why: The holding-period line is right: long-term means held MORE than one year, counted from the day after purchase, so a sale on the first anniversary is still short-term and the day after is long-term; the leap-day rule (anniversary on 28 February, so 1 March is long-term) agrees. Gain per lot = shares × (price − cost) × multiplier is right. Three faults: (1) a lot whose cost per share is not above zero is skipped, so a lot transferred in with no basis vanishes from the split and the total disagrees with unrealizedGain (MK-PF-F-005) for the same holding; (2) with no price it returns zeros, which reads as 'no gain'; (3) a lot with no valid date is called short-term, which is a guess (it may well be long-term).
formula_checks.should_be: For each lot with shares: gain = shares × (price − cost per share) × multiplier; long-term when the sale day (today) is after the first anniversary of purchase, short-term otherwise. If any lot holding shares has no cost on record, or no valid date, the part it belongs to (and the total) is unknown and is not shown as a number. With no price: no answer.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRS Publication 550 (for 2025 returns), 'Holding Period': more than one year is long-term; count from the day after acquisition; the day of sale is included. Agreement with MK-PF-F-005.

formula_checks.name: totalROI
formula_checks.why: Gain ÷ cost is a return on money paid, which for a holding bought in several lots at different times is close to a money-weighted figure, not a time-weighted one. Owner decision Q16 (updated 2026-10-04) says every return in the app is time-weighted. For one lot the two agree; for lots bought at different prices they do not. It matters on screen because buildPerformance (MK-PF-F-014) uses this as the period return of a holding bought inside the window. Refusing with no price or no cost is right.
formula_checks.should_be: Return since purchase = the time-weighted return of the holding from its first purchase: chain-link the price at each purchase (piece = price just before the next purchase ÷ price after the last), which for a holding with no sales and no distributions equals today's price ÷ the price at the first purchase − 1. Refuse with no price or no cost.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision Q16 (2026-10-04, DEC-1669): every return is time-weighted.

formula_checks.name: earliestPurchaseDate
formula_checks.why: The earliest dated lot is the day the holding first became the person's money; ignoring undated lots and returning nothing when none is dated is right. Low: 'valid date' is not defined on the card; if it means only the year-month-day shape (as MK-ST-F-080 isDay does), an impossible date such as 2023-02-30 would count.

formula_checks.name: realizedFromLedger
formula_checks.why: First-in-first-out matching within one account and one ticker, gain = proceeds − cost of the matched shares, and 'this year' by sale date are all right (FIFO is the IRS default when specific shares are not identified). But unlike costBasis, marketValue and capGains, this formula never applies the contract multiplier (MK-PF-F-031): an option sold for $5.45 a share after buying at $3.20 shows a realised gain 100 times too small. Two smaller gaps: a sale only partly matched is counted for its matched part and also tallied as 'without a cost', and the card does not say whether it also counts in 'sales counted'; and 'with a price' does not say what happens to a buy at a price of 0 (a gift or a transfer recorded at zero), which would make its shares look free.
formula_checks.should_be: Gain on a sale = matched shares × (sale price − cost per share of the matched lots) × the contract multiplier of that holding (MK-PF-F-031). Say whether a partly matched sale counts in 'sales counted'.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRS Publication 550 (2025): FIFO when shares are not identified; consistency with MK-PF-F-002 / MK-PF-F-031 (an option premium is per share, × 100 per contract).

formula_checks.name: quantityUnit
formula_checks.why: The person's own unit first, then coins / contracts / ounces by kind, then shares, is the right label rule. Low: the registry tags MK-XS-I-004 (quantity) and MK-XS-I-055 (account wrapper) do not fit a function that reads only the kind and the unit.

formula_checks.name: quantityWithUnit
formula_checks.why: Quantity followed by its unit, singular at exactly 1, is right for ordinary holdings. It is silent on a negative quantity: a short option (a covered call written against shares) is held as −1 contract, and the rule 'exactly 1' prints '-1 contracts'. English takes the singular for one of anything, positive or negative. Low: the registry tag 'holding price' does not fit.
formula_checks.should_be: The unit loses its final s when the quantity is exactly 1 or exactly −1.
